description.narrative:
Project's Overall Goal (longer term goal) is: Women and men in Ukraine see tangible improvements to their standard of living and governance quality due to better implementation and funding behind the SDGs and their targets as adopted for Ukraine.
The Project will have one Output (immediate objective): Ukraine has a well-conceived and tested system for mainstreaming SDGs into policy-documents and tracking government-funded SDG Target-related activities backed up by improved governance dialogue and political will.

UNDP har ansökt om ett stöd på 3,6 miljoner kronor för att genomföra projektet 'SDC Bridge Ukraine' under perioden 2021-2023.
Projektet kommer att stödja etableringen av ett system för att integrera Agenda 2030 och de globala målen för hållbar utveckling (Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs) i den ukrainska regeringens policydokument och i uppföljningen av statligt finansierade SDG-relaterade aktiviteter i Ukraina. Detta ska göras genom a) stöd till utvecklingen av en strategi för hur den globala målen ska integreras i regeringens policies (i samordning med nyckelaktörer), b) rådgivning till regeringen i utformningen av program och uppföljnings-och koordineringsmekanismer c) strategisk planering och finansiering för hållbar utveckling på nationell och regional nivå i Ukraina, d) att stärka dialogen om genomförandet av de globala målen mellan regeringen, parlamentet och givare (med utgångspunkt i givarkoordineringsstrukturen i Ukraina), och e) att bidra till att anpassa regeringens strategidokument till Agenda 2030 och de globala målen.
Insatsens totala budget är 5,1 miljoner kronor, varav 3,6 miljoner kronor utgör det svenska bidraget (varav 8% kommer att gå till UNDP General Management Support Cost).

United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has applied to Swedish Embassy in Ukraine for funding of 3,6 million SEK to carry out the 'SDC Bridge Ukraine' Project in Ukraine during the period 2021-2023.
The intervention aims at establishing a well-conceived and tested system for mainstreaming Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into policy-documents and tracking government-funded SDG Target-related activities in Ukraine by a) elaborating a conceptual approach to Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) mainstreaming into national policies, strategies and programming process in coordination with key stakeholders; b) advising the Government on designing adequate programming and tracking instruments and coherent coordination mechanisms; c) promoting strategic planning and financing for sustainable development at the national and regional level in Ukraine; d) strengthening the dialogue on SDG implementation between the Government, the Parliament and development partners (building on the existing three-level international technical assistance (ITA) coordination system); and e) contributing to aligning high-level strategic policy documents with the SDG framework and Agenda 2030.
The intervention’s total budget is 5,1 million SEK, out of which 3,6 million SEK is Swedish contribution (out of which 8% will amount for UNDP General Management Support Cost).

sector.narrative: Public sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
Some of the project lessons can be summarized below:
Lack of the effective coordination mechanism for the SDGs implementation creates challenges for the respective results achievement. The SDG BRIDGE Project was designed upon the request of the Prime Minister of Ukraine and at the same time at the initiative of the Vice-Prime-Minister on European and Euro-Atlantic Integration. This resulted in multiple, sometimes conflicting requests and different understanding of the approaches and division of responsibilities to address the proposed actions in SDG mainstreaming and establishment of the SDG Office. To enhance coordination mechanisms related to SDGs implementation within the Government, efficient support to all involved stakeholders, including the SCMU and VPMs Office, was critical.
Effective collaboration on SDG implementation and incorporation into national strategic policy is subject to an important "tone/message from the top''. Leadership of the Prime Minister, VPM and senior management of the SCMU was critical for the introduction of SDGs into national policy documents, e.g National Economic Strategy 2030. There was a widespread belief that already existing procedures were good enough to implement SDGs despite solid evidence showing that old procedures did not allow to fully monitor progress on SDGs achievement and coordinate implementation of Agenda 2030. That is why it is crucial to have support of the top-level decision-makers to achieve results and ensure the sustainability of the process.
In the times of rapidly shifting policy priorities, and institutional changes, SDG BRIDGE Project provided a platform for institutional memory on the sustainable development agenda and could serve a desirable purpose when being adaptive in terms of methodologies and tools, at the same time, incorporating SDGs tasks and indicators. As the Sustainable Development Agenda continues being the guidance for foreign financial and technical assistance incoming to Ukraine, it becomes a solid argument for attracting attention and is welcomed among policy developers. Although 2017 localised SDGs provide a good strategic path for national planning documents, recent war-related societal, economic and institutional developments require further revision / enhancement of localised Goals for Ukraine. National authorities applied this approach, being assisted by the SDG BRIDGE Project, which allowed for better operational and strategic incorporation of SDGs into Ukraine`s policies, as well as drafting new SDG targets and monitoring tools. This is especially relevant for health care, education, institutional resilience, economic (SMEs development) areas, peace and justice aspects.
Civil society and youth communities engagement is instrumental to support effective Sustainable Development agenda solutions and find innovative strategic communication tools. It should be strongly applied at the stage of preparing new policy recommendations to the Government, even before the formal policy cycle starts, including stakeholders consultations, which also allows a room for civil society participation.
